sections.html:
You'll find the Recorder at 123 Wyoming Avenue, Suite 218, Scranton. Call 570-963-6775. The office keeps 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. hours, though recording submissions end at 3:45 p.m.

A signed deed can reach the office three ways: carried in, dropped in the box in the main lobby of the Government Center, or sent by U.S. Mail. Title companies often skip all three and file electronically through Simplifile, CSC or ePN, the vendors the county lists on its Recorder of Deeds page.

Besides recording and indexing property documents, the Recorder collects realty transfer tax on behalf of the state, the municipality and the school district. A seller reaches this office at the very end, once the deed has been signed and notarized.

Lackawanna's written recording requirements have tracked national PRIA document standards since September 1, 2024. A closing package that comes back usually lacks one of the items below.

  • Paper size of 8.5 by 11 inches (8.5 by 14 is tolerated), type no smaller than 12 point, and margins of at least one inch on every page.
  • Original signatures in dark ink. Handwriting isn't allowed anywhere else on the page, and highlighter marks aren't allowed at all.
  • A complete legal description naming the municipality, county and state, plus the county tax parcel number. The Assessment Office certifies each parcel number before the deed is recorded, and mailed packages are forwarded there first.
  • An acknowledgment taken by a notary or other authorized officer, with the date, the signer's name, the notary's signature and the commission expiration date.
  • A Certificate of Residence signed by the buyer, giving a precise address.
  • Written dollar amounts that match the numbers, since consideration is checked against the transfer tax paid.

Re-recording won't repair a deed. A Corrective Deed is the only fix, and it must carry a Statement of Value, an explanation, and a full copy of the deed being corrected.

Bring a check for the exact amount. Credit cards aren't taken, overages aren't refunded, and every check should have the submitter's address printed on it.

Payment rules from the recording requirements sheet, revised August 2024

Payee is the Lackawanna County Recorder of Deeds. The office refuses a check whose memo line points to some other land document, and it may ask for ID to confirm the address printed on a check.

Base amounts vary with the number of pages, names and parcels. Use the fee calculator on the county's Recorder page, or phone the office, before you write the check.

sections.h2: Realty transfer tax on a sale
sections.html:
The tax is taken at the counter when the deed is recorded. The state's share is 1 percent of the value, and both buyer and seller answer to the Department of Revenue for it. The municipality and school district add their own local portions.

Certain transfers are exempt, such as some between relatives and property passing under a will or by intestacy. Even so, the exemption has to be spelled out in the deed or on a fully completed Statement of Value.

  • Land in several municipalities: the deed lists each one's percentage and dollar amount in whole numbers, supported by a Statement of Value.
  • Wrong location on the deed: the submitter owes the correct tax to the correct municipality and must chase the refund from the one paid in error.
  • Easements: these need a Statement of Value too, and it counts toward the page total.

The combined court and AOPC portion of the surcharge on every recording is now $41.25, up from $40.25. It followed a state budget change signed on November 12, 2025, and the Recorder began collecting the higher amount on November 17, 2025. Packages mailed in with the old amount were sent back to be redone.

Since January 1, 2026, attachments on e-recorded documents, such as a Corrective Deed or Deed of Trust, cost an extra $0.50 per page, because the office must print them for the Department of Revenue. Documents brought in, dropped off or mailed don't pick up that per-page charge.

If your closing package was prepared from an older checklist, ask the office for the current total before sending a check.

sections.h2: The Lackawanna County reassessment and your sale
sections.html:
The county finished its first full reassessment in nearly 60 years in 2025, moving values off 1968 levels to current market values. A court ordered it after a 2022 resident lawsuit. The Assessment Office says the county millage rate fell from 89.98 to 5.79 mills to keep the change revenue-neutral.

The county describes the result as roughly a third of owners paying more, a third paying less and a third about the same. A quarterly payment option was introduced for property tax bills. An old tax bill says little about what a buyer will pay now, so pull the current assessment record before you list.

Assessment appeals open again on April 1, 2027, and the next Clean & Green application window starts March 1, 2027. The county also posts a form under Act 29 of 2026 for owners of rentals, LLCs, trusts and other entity-held property bought on or after September 18, 2026.

Lackawanna County has an estimated 216,502 residents as of July 2025 and 100,686 housing units. The owner-occupied rate is 65.4% for 2020 to 2024, and the median owner-occupied home value is $201,800. Median gross rent is $1,007.

Scranton is the county seat and Carbondale is the other city. If you price a vacant house in winter, plan for snow-season showings and heating costs.

sections.h2: What to bring to a Lackawanna County closing
sections.html:
Gather these items first and the counter clerk has little reason to turn you away.

  • The deed, signed in original ink and acknowledged, with the notary stamp clear and nothing typed or written onto it.
  • The county tax parcel number and a full legal description.
  • A signed Certificate of Residence from the buyer.
  • A completed Statement of Value if any tax is excused or the price is not shown on the deed.
  • A check for the exact total, with the submitter's address printed on it.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the recorded original mailed back.

Get it to the counter by 3:45 p.m. on a business day, or let the title company file it electronically.

faqs.q: Can I pay for recording in Lackawanna County with a credit card?
faqs.a: No. The office doesn't accept credit cards. Bring a check for the exact amount, made out to the Lackawanna County Recorder of Deeds. A single check may cover both the recording fee and the transfer tax.

faqs.q: What time does Lackawanna County stop recording deeds?
faqs.a: Recording ends at 3:45 p.m. The office stays open until 4:00 p.m. and opens at 9:00 a.m. A deed that arrives after 3:45 waits for the next business day.

faqs.q: Does a Lackawanna County deed need a parcel number?
faqs.a: Yes. Every document that relates directly to real estate must carry the county tax parcel number, and the Assessment Office certifies it before recording. A mailed package is forwarded to that office first.

faqs.q: Can a mistake in a recorded deed be fixed by recording it again?
faqs.a: No. Deeds can only be corrected with a Corrective Deed. It must include a Statement of Value, a reason for the correction, and a complete copy of the deed being corrected.

faqs.q: Who pays realty transfer tax when a Lackawanna County house sells?
faqs.a: Buyer and seller are both liable for the state 1 percent tax. Your sales contract can say who actually pays. The Recorder collects it with the deed and passes it on to the state, the municipality and the school district.
